channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Brookfield’s Flatt Says AI ‘Slowing Down Anyway’ as Builders Can’t Keep Up
item.description: Brookfield Corp. Chief Executive Officer Bruce Flatt said the artificial-intelligence race is already slowing because developers can’t build enough infrastructure to keep pace with what AI companies are demanding.
item.dc:creator: Layan Odeh

item.title: Hugging Face AI Hack Shows Humans Can Keep the Technology in Check
item.description: The rhetoric focused on the technology’s existential threat overshadows more correctable issues
item.dc:creator: Davey Alba

item.title: EQT Is Backing $2 Billion Small-Battery Push to Enable AI
item.description: EQT Infrastructure is backing a $2 billion small-battery investment to slash power costs for industrial consumers and help data centers get connected faster to the largest US electricity grid.
item.dc:creator: Naureen S. Malik

item.title: Trump and Xi Jinping Face Off on AI as White House Meeting Nears
item.description: The two countries don’t even agree on AI’s biggest threats
item.dc:creator: Saritha Rai

item.title: SoftBank Boosts Credit Line to $6.5 Billion as AI Debts Mount
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. secured an additional $450 million to increase the size of an existing credit line to $6.5 billion, people familiar with the matter said, giving the Japanese conglomerate more financial flexibility as it expands investments in artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang

item.title: Software Stocks Get New Life From Strong Earnings, AI Warnings
item.description: Software stocks were basically left for dead earlier this year as investors bet that the business was doomed by the emergence of artificial intelligence. But it turns out that imminent demise was greatly exaggerated.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: AI Boom Risks a ‘Corporate Extinction Event’: Paul
item.description: Sherry Paul, managing director and private wealth advisor at Morgan Stanley, says companies that fail to embrace AI risk being overtaken by competitors that use the technology to boost productivity and profitability. “We move into what I call the corporate extinction event,” Paul says on “Bloomberg Surveillance,” comparing the disruption to Netflix overtaking Blockbuster. This interview aired Sept. 17, 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Global Agency on AI Would Be Useful, Ireland’s Harris Says
item.description: A global agency for artificial intelligence would be a positive development, Irish Finance Minister Simon Harris said.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Valero, Kamil Kowalcze and Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Traders Wary Of Rising AI Risks: Market Snapshot
item.description: The global debate over artificial intelligence risks entered a new phase this week amid clashing views from tech executives over whether frontier labs should slow the development of the technology. Leaders of Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceX and Google DeepMind put forward the need for self-regulation checks on growth that give AI models more control. Meanwhile, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta said they're developing tools to check, control and regulate AI risks as US President Donald Trump called the alerts a "hoax". The call for caution saw a rotation out of tech stocks at the start of the week as investors questioned whether there's a need to reprice the pace of the booming AI buildout. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: SoftBank Adds $21 Billion to AI Firepower in New Debt Deals
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp. is closing out the week with nearly $21 billion in potential fresh borrowings as it builds out its artificial intelligence financing capacity. It’s also looking to raise another $10 billion to $20 billion next week in a separate jumbo bond deal.
item.dc:creator: Janice Huang, Kari Lindberg and Min Jeong Lee

item.title: Huawei Speeds Up Launch of New AI Chip
item.description: Huawei is accelerating the debut of its next-generation AI chip by several months, aiming to replace Nvidia in China and compete on the global stage. The Ascend 960DT chip will now be launched in the first quarter of 2027. Another variant of the new series, dubbed 960PR, will be delivered in the third quarter. Bloomberg's Anthony Stephens reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: GCash Owner Gets Approval for Up to $1.5 Billion Philippines IPO
item.description: The company behind GCash, the biggest mobile wallet app in the Philippines, received approval from the country’s stock exchange operator of an initial public offering of as much as 92.3 billion pesos ($1.47 billion), clearing the final regulatory hurdle for a record debut.
item.dc:creator: Neil Jerome Morales

item.title: Chinese Robotics Suppliers Rise on Tesla Visit Report
item.description: Shares of Chinese robotics‑component suppliers climbed after a local report said Tesla Inc. teams had arrived in the country to audit suppliers and place additional orders to boost production of its Optimus humanoid model.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Waymo Plans to Offer Paid Robotaxi Rides in Singapore in 2028
item.description: Waymo plans to offer its robotaxi service in Singapore in 2028, the latest in a string of domestic and international expansions by the Alphabet Inc. unit.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Lung

item.title: Indian Project Financier’s Data Center Loans Top $1.2 Billion
item.description: India’s top state-run infrastructure financier has sanctioned loans upwards of 30 billion rupees ($313 million) each to at least four data centers, reflecting the nation’s push to participate in the artificial intelligence buildout.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Das and Divya Patil

item.title: Traders Eye Xi-Trump Meet for Clues on AI Rivalry, Yuan Outlook
item.description: Artificial intelligence, a lingering trade war and the yuan will likely dominate the agenda of the upcoming US-China summit, with focus on whether the two nations can reach concessions or put guardrails around key areas of competition, analysts say.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: India’s Quick-Commerce Architect Takes a Long Bet
item.description:
The man who transformed how urban India eats, dines, and shops, Deepinder Goyal built his food delivery startup Zomato into one of the country’s biggest consumer technology companies, Eternal. At the height of its success, Goyal stepped away from the day-to-day running of the company he built, to turn his attention to a very different set of challenges with a much longer horizon.
In an exclusive interview on his sprawling residence in Delhi, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with Goyal about the never-ending journeys of founders, his current pursuits, and his quest for a different kind of eternity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India’s Quick-Commerce Disruptor Stays Calm on AI ‘Myth’
item.description:
Widely seen as the architect of the instant delivery model in India, Deepinder Goyal stays confident that the platforms he has built up under Eternal, such as Zomato and Blinkit, can harness AI for their customers better than general AI models can.
As Goyal steps away from day-to-day operations of the company he has built, Bloomberg’s Haslinda Amin speaks with him in an exclusive interview from his sprawling private residence in Delhi, about his journey thus far and the pursuit of a different kind of eternity. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Palantir Hires Former UK Labour Veteran With NHS Deal in Limbo
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc. has hired Tom Watson, a former Labour deputy leader, as a new executive in the UK, where it faces a barrage of criticism threatening a major contract.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Alex Morales

item.title: India’s Chip Plan Investment Pledges Hit $12 Billion
item.description: India has received investment pledges of as much as $12 billion from global and local investors within months of launching its new semiconductor policy, marking an acceleration in its efforts to become a chip-making nation.
item.dc:creator: Sankalp Phartiyal
